key_insight: A fast ML-based surrogate replaces computationally expensive 1-D arterial solvers to deliver personalized, real-time predictions of blood flow and hemodynamic indices, while estimating hard-to-measure parameters (e.g., terminal resistance/compliance). This enables rapid, population-scale or bedside hemodynamic analysis without sacrificing clinically relevant fidelity.
problem_solved: 1-D arterial models are accurate but too slow and parameter-sensitive for large cohorts, real-time applications, or clinical personalization—especially when key boundary parameters are difficult to measure clinically.
method: Train a surrogate model (data-driven emulator) to approximate a validated 1-D arterial blood-flow solver across physiologically realistic parameter ranges.

Personalize the surrogate to individuals via inverse parameter estimation/calibration (optimization or Bayesian inference) to infer terminal resistance, compliance and other patient-specific parameters from limited clinical measurements.
Validate surrogate fidelity and quantify uncertainty against the full 1-D solver and/or measured clinical data to ensure clinically relevant accuracy while enabling orders-of-magnitude speed-up.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners this demonstrates how surrogate modeling + parameter estimation can transform physics-based biomedical simulations into real-time, scalable tools for digital twins, cohort studies, and clinical decision support, integrating seamlessly with ML pipelines and uncertainty-aware workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: clinical inputs → parameter calibration → surrogate model → real-time hemodynamic outputs

Example dashboard mockup: individualized pressure/flow waveforms and derived metrics ready for clinical use
paper_title: Real-Time Surrogate Modeling for Personalized Blood Flow Prediction and Hemodynamic Analysis
paper_authors: Sokratis J. Anagnostopoulos, George Rovas, Vasiliki Bikia, Theodore G. Papaioannou, Athanase D. Protogerou
